tasks.title: Daily primary-source SOTA scanner and comparable target ledger
tasks.objective: Implement a deterministic daily discovery pipeline that records the best public inference result for every supported exact model and compiles a SparkPipe target of at least 110% of the best genuinely comparable result.
non_goals: Treat vendor marketing, anonymous screenshots, or unmatched benchmark shapes as SOTA evidence
Claim SparkPipe performance from an external result
Silently compare different checkpoints, quality levels, hardware counts, batches, contexts, speculation settings, or timing boundaries
acceptance: Every observation binds source URL, retrieval time, source revision or publication date, exact checkpoint, quality mode, hardware, topology, batch, prompt and output lengths, context occupancy, speculation, metric, timing boundary, and evidence class
Primary official repositories, documentation, papers, benchmark artifacts, and reproducible issue receipts are preferred; secondary claims remain quarantined and cannot set the target
The comparator emits COMPARABLE, PARTIAL, or INCOMPARABLE with field-level reasons and never normalizes missing facts into invented values
The 110% target is emitted only for a comparable cell and uses explicit metric direction and units
Offline fixtures make tests deterministic while the production command can refresh sources from the network
Supported models include DSV4 Flash, DSV4 Pro, GLM 5.2, K3, MiniMax H3, Qwen 3.8 Pro, and Qwen 3.8 27B

tasks.title: Auditable benchmark protocol and plus-10 target compiler
tasks.objective: Freeze the benchmark cells and statistical decision rules used to prove that SparkPipe matches or exceeds a comparable SOTA result and reaches the 110% economic target.
non_goals: Declare a win from analytical rooflines
Credit more accelerators without reporting per-device efficiency and fleet throughput separately
acceptance: Cells cover B1 through B1024 with an explicit context/output envelope rather than assuming every Cartesian point fits
Comparisons require the same exact checkpoint and an explicit quality-equivalence gate before performance
End-to-end, engine-only, and isolated-kernel boundaries remain separate
Paired randomized A/B, warmup, sample count, confidence interval, output parity, power state, clocks, and thermal state are recorded
The compiler reports SOTA parity, 110% target, observed gap, and uncertainty without extrapolating unmeasured cells

tasks.title: Profile-to-work-order compiler
tasks.objective: Turn a no-drop end-to-end profile and current SOTA gap into narrowly scoped optimization tasks ranked by exposed wall-time opportunity, implementation risk, and hardware test cost.
non_goals: Rank summed overlapping kernel times as wall time
Generate tasks that share a broad model-directory write lock
Accept isolated microbenchmark wins as model wins
acceptance: Every generated task names one bottleneck, exact source files, a falsifiable hypothesis, control and candidate commands, rollback, numerical gate, and end-to-end A/B gate
Tasks are split until implementer write sets are disjoint
Expected gain is analytical and cannot satisfy acceptance
Rejected experiments remain searchable so agents do not repeat known losses

tasks.title: DSV4 Flash current SOTA gap and no-drop bottleneck refresh
tasks.objective: Refresh the exact DSV4 Flash TP4 performance target, reproduce the best retained SparkPipe baseline, and produce a no-drop profile that identifies exposed—not merely summed—wall time.
non_goals: Treat branch-level receipts as merged-main qualification
acceptance: The control is the exact current-main build and exact GA checkpoint with output parity
The profile separates GPU busy union, exposed idle, collectives, host/runtime gaps, and overlapping kernel categories
At least three disjoint implementation work orders are emitted with source-level write sets
Hardware-unavailable runs remain BLOCKED_HARDWARE and cannot fabricate profile data

tasks.title: DSV4 Flash highest-exposed-wall-time optimization slice
tasks.objective: Implement the highest-ranked source-disjoint DSV4 Flash work order and retain it only if exact output and paired end-to-end performance beat the current-main control.
non_goals: Keep code for an isolated-kernel win that loses end to end
Lower numerical quality to gain speed
acceptance: Candidate is bitwise exact where the contract is exact and within unchanged tolerances elsewhere
Three or more randomized interleaved full-request A/B pairs are positive in aggregate and report every pair
The result updates the gap to comparable SOTA and the 110% target
A regression or inconclusive result produces a rejection receipt and no production source change

tasks.title: K3 sharding and runtime correctness blockers
tasks.objective: Port only the reviewed K3 sharder corrections and fix the layer-92 classification and premature tp_collective hard requirement before any K3 performance work.
non_goals: Import unified operational scripts or temporary artifacts
Optimize kernels before the exact layer gates pass
acceptance: kda_decay_bias, kda_head_log_scale, and routed_norm_weight use checkpoint-derived sharding rules
Layer 92 has an explicit regression fixture
The device-collective path is reachable without a contradictory host collective requirement
No readiness or speed claim is emitted without a real checkpoint and target receipt

tasks.title: GLM 5.2 real-pack correctness path
tasks.objective: Extract the reviewed GLM 5.2 runtime slices without mixed unified artifacts, wire the stagepack resolver into production ingestion, and make the validator consume a real exact pack.
non_goals: Use synthetic weights as readiness evidence
Begin performance tuning before checkpoint parity
acceptance: Production and validation resolve the same exact stagepack identity
Synthetic and real-pack evidence are labeled separately
One complete real-weight layer matches the authoritative implementation
Performance tasks remain blocked until the numerical gate passes

tasks.title: Qwen 3.8 27B one-Spark SOTA gap and bottleneck profile
tasks.objective: Bind the working one-Spark Qwen 3.8 27B path to its exact checkpoint, refresh comparable SOTA cells, and profile B1 plus the first useful batching cells.
non_goals: Compare FP8 and BF16 storage without reporting quality and memory differences
Modify kernels in the profiling task
acceptance: B1 control reproduces exact output and current-main speed within declared variance
B2, B4, B8, and B16 are measured or explicitly capacity-blocked
Profile identifies exposed GPU, memory, host, graph, speculation, and sampling time
Work orders distinguish quality-preserving compute changes from storage-codec experiments

tasks.title: GLM 5.2 post-correctness SOTA performance program
tasks.objective: After exact real-pack correctness, establish the first end-to-end baseline and execute the highest-exposed-wall-time work order against a comparable SOTA target.
non_goals: Claim SOTA from an isolated CUDA kernel
acceptance: The first receipt is an honest baseline even when far below target
Optimization retains real-checkpoint numerical parity
End-to-end A/B and current comparable SOTA gap are both reported
Hardware and topology are exact and reproducible

tasks.title: K3 post-correctness SOTA performance program

acceptance: Baseline includes all ranks, collectives, sampling, and streamed client observation
Output identity and pack freshness are proven before timing

SOTA parity and 110% target remain cell-specific
